inputs.text: When Tom Homan won’t rule out immigration enforcement at polling places, alarm is entirely reasonable—not evidence that Democrats oppose the law. The prospect can intimidate voters, especially people in immigrant communities, and make a basic democratic right feel risky. “Orderly” elections mean people can cast a ballot without fear; they don’t require turning polling places into sites of immigration enforcement. Confusing messages from the administration only deepen that fear. Protecting equal access to the vote should come before using “law and order” rhetoric to dismiss those concerns.
